text: Python already has functions that pause: async def and await. doeff pauses with yield instead. Both print the same line. So why yield?
At an await, the call names the code that answers. That code runs right there, as part of the same chain of calls.
At a yield, the call names an operation. ReadName is a value, not code. greet pauses, and the nearest handler around it answers.
In asyncio, every request goes to one place: the event loop at the top. The coroutines in between only pass it through.
In doeff, each caller installs handlers around any part of a program. Add titled in between, and the first greeting says Dr. Ada. greet does not change.
A handler also holds the rest of the function, k. It can resume it, keep it to run tasks, or end the run without it.
Async libraries still work. Await hands one coroutine to a handler, and the event loop moves from above the program to behind that handler.
async and await are an effect system with one handler, fixed at the top. doeff lets every caller install their own.
